claude.sample_unit: test radiographs (scaphoid crops), each perturbed across 44 degradation datasets

links.outcome: Classifier accuracy under perturbed inputs (blur, noise, JPEG, CLAHE, resizing, screenshots) versus clean images
links.effect: Accuracy fell from 92.03% clean as perturbation severity increased; Gaussian blur σ=3.0 gave 72.0%, resize_400 71.9%, CLAHE clip 5 77.0%, ImageJ screenshot 78.1%.
links.quote: However, as the perturbations increased in severity, image features deteriorated further, and model performance declined.

links.outcome: Silent performance loss from degraded or low-resolution input images
links.effect: Resolution reduction and screenshots cut accuracy (MicroDicom 900×1050 to 550×780: 86.3% to 82.8%; ImageJ 78.1%); no input quality check was tested.
links.quote: The only difference between the datasets Screenshot_MicroDicom_1 and Screenshot_MicroDicom_2 was the resolution; changing the resolution from 900×1050 to 550×780 pixels resulted in an accuracy reduction from 86.3% to 82.8%.

links.outcome: Performance variation across acquisition sources and display software
links.effect: The model was robust to 12-bit rescaling methods (<1% accuracy drop), but viewer-specific screenshot capture reduced accuracy (ImageJ 78.1% vs MicroDicom_1 82.8% at similar resolution).
links.quote: This suggests that viewer-specific display or resampling algorithms during screenshot capture may also influence model performance.

unlisted_practices: Training with augmentation matched to expected degradations, such as CLAHE, blur, and grayscale noise, to improve robustness
Using PSNR and SSIM image-quality metrics to predict model performance
Quality control of image resolution and compression before AI inference

openai.sample_unit: radiographs in the independent test set, repeatedly perturbed

links.effect: Clean accuracy was 92.03%; Gaussian blur_3.0 accuracy 0.7203, Resize_400 0.7188, CLAHE_5 0.7703, and Screenshot_ImageJ 0.7812.
links.quote: For images with PSNR values between 35 and 50, linear regression analysis revealed that Gaussian blurring was associated with a 5% to 12% decrease in accuracy compared with other nongeometric transformation techniques.

links.effect: Changing screenshot resolution from 900×1050 to 550×780 pixels reduced accuracy from 86.3% to 82.8%; Screenshot_ImageJ accuracy was 78.1%.
links.quote: The only difference between the datasets Screenshot_MicroDicom_1 and Screenshot_MicroDicom_2 was the resolution; changing the resolution from 900×1050 to 550×780 pixels resulted in an accuracy reduction from 86.3% to 82.8%.

links.outcome: fracture classification accuracy under image perturbations
links.effect: Accuracy declined from 0.9203 on clean images to 0.7203 under Gaussian blur (sigma=3.0) and 0.7703 under CLAHE, where recall dropped to 0.5390, while Gaussian blur decreased accuracy by 5% to 12%.
links.quote: Model accuracy declined with increasing perturbation severity, but the extent varied across perturbation types.

screen.practice: image quality control (resolution and blur checks)
screen.reason: The study empirically tests AI robustness against specific image perturbations (noise, compression, resolution loss) to evaluate image quality control safeguards before diagnostic deployment.
